### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via newTabUrl (literal, a string literal in sections))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via newTabUrl (literal, a string literal in sections))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4dabc85fc0cc0334be4a4b8bf5888ad084ca3149` — the merge of head `78e8f97515f54992d16469102d21f461840d42a0` into base `0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4dabc85fc0cc0334be4a4b8bf5888ad084ca3149 && git checkout 4dabc85fc0cc0334be4a4b8bf5888ad084ca3149
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b 78e8f97515f54992d16469102d21f461840d42a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b && git merge --no-ff 78e8f97515f54992d16469102d21f461840d42a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `78e8f97515f54992d16469102d21f461840d42a0`
Local-runs: none

Outside this scope — the four `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` bundles — is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Round 2 of record 6470108120 on #27252 (merged 13:42Z as `c13ef04c3`, queued before that record posted). Inputs: card #26924 (every comment through the landing note 6471217433), PR #27282 body, file list (9 paths) and net diff against merge base `7858c1d16` (+62/-8), and the check-runs on this head. The head reviewed is the PR's current head: two commits on `7858c1d16` — `0c704ce93` (entry, changeset, labels, JSDoc; 8 paths) and `78e8f9751` (one sentence in `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`). The order named `0c704ce93`; its runs were cancelled by the concurrency group when `78e8f9751` was pushed at 14:29Z (`TypeScript Type Check` closed as `failure` on cancelled lanes, `Build Core` and the UI contexts `cancelled`), so that head carries no gate verdicts and no record can be rendered on it; the queue guard reads the record for the current head. Gates on `78e8f9751`, read to completion (54 check-runs, 0 pending at 14:53Z): every one of the ten required contexts is `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (check:docs, check:generated and the ADR-0087 gate ride in it), `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` — and `Lint UI` is `skipped` by its paths filter (no `ui/**` on the file list). `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes` and `Spec property liveness` are `success`; no check-run is `failure` or `cancelled`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The FAIL item of 6470108120 is closed — right.** `18.ui-action-new-tab-url-path-refused.ts` exports a `SemanticMigration` with the four load-bearing fields (`types.ts:99-112`): `surface` names the `action` documents (standalone, `actions[]`, type-level) whose `newTabUrl` does not start with `/`; `replacement` names both remedies — the backend path, or a `type: 'url'` action with `target: 'https://…${ctx.recordId}'` and `openIn: 'new-tab'` — and states "NOT mechanically convertible, so this entry is a structured TODO", with the reason a conversion is not written (changes `type`, drops the action's own handler, replaces an auth-enforcing endpoint); `reason` states the origin-prefix behaviour (`consoleServerAction.ts:209`, unchanged) and why the set was closed rather than widened; `acceptanceCriteria` restates the stored-row behaviour #27252 pinned. Same shape as the precedent entry, `conversionIds` rightly omitted (it judges no mechanical edit). File prefix `18.` matches `PROTOCOL_VERSION` `18.0.0`; `build-migration-registry.ts` discovers the directory, so the entry enters `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic` and `migrations.test.ts:705-706` holds that the chain emits every such id — the entry reaches `os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide with no companion detector owed (the precedent has none either).
- **The marker — right in substance, verified by hand.** `.changeset/26924-new-tab-url-d3-entry.md` carries exactly one marker, `adr-0087: registered ui-action-new-tab-url-path-refused`, and the id resolves to the entry added in this diff. Note for the record: this changeset declares no breaking change, and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` judges only changesets that do (its G1 battery: "a non-breaking changeset is not this gate's business"), so the PR body's reading "exit 0 (reads the `registered` marker against the entry)" is a gate that did not look, not one that agreed. The id was checked here instead: entry file, exported `id`, file name and marker agree. Nothing to change — declaring the changeset BREAKING to make the gate look would be false.
- **Accept set, authorable surface, published schema — unchanged; right.** `action.zod.ts` moves two JSDoc lines only (the stored-row paragraph now names the D3 entry); `.describe()` is byte-identical, so the JSON Schema, authorable-surface shards and generated reference pages do not move. `action.form.ts` changes the `newTabUrl` label only; help text and `visibleWhen` unchanged. No `ui/**` change; the renderer's behaviour #27252 documented still holds.
- **Form label — right, closes the should-fix.** "New-tab path" (en, regenerated from source), 「新标签页路径」 (zh-CN), 「新しいタブのパス」 (ja-JP), "Ruta de pestaña nueva" (es-ES), keys unchanged, the translated values hand-edited as the Documentation Guardrails row prescribes. `git grep` on the head for "New-tab URL", 「新标签页 URL」, 「タブの URL」 and "URL de pestaña" across packages, ui, content and skills (CHANGELOGs excluded): 0 hits.
- **The docs sentence (`78e8f9751`) — right.** `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx:110` now says `newTabUrl` "skips the round-trip with a path on this backend, starting with `/` (`{recordId}` placeholder); an absolute URL is refused, so an external page is a `type: 'url'` action with `openIn: 'new-tab'`" — the same meaning as the schema's `.describe()`, the form help and the skills sentence, and the page is in a hand-written tree (not `references/`, not `releases/`), so the edit is allowed there and belongs with the change that falsified the old wording.
- **Nothing #27252 shipped regresses — right.** Nine paths: one new entry, one new changeset, one JSDoc edit, one label, one docs sentence, four translation bundles. The regex, prescription, describe, skills sentence, liveness rows, dashboard prose and citations are untouched on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset — right: no key, value or meaning an author can write moves. `@objectstack/spec` **patch** (a registry entry and a JSDoc line in a published package) and `@objectstack/platform-objects` **patch** (label strings in the shipped bundles) — right; no `skip-changeset`.
- **Superseding the merged disposition — right, and the only available form.** `.changeset/26924-new-tab-url-backend-path.md` (the `not-required` note) and `.changeset/26924-platform-objects-new-tab-url-help.md` are both still present on `origin/main`, so neither has been consumed by a release: the two notes ship in the same `changeset version`. Editing the merged note here is refused by `check-empty-changeset`'s foreign-changeset rule (#17712: a PR may not MODIFY or DELETE a `.changeset/*.md` that exists on the merge base and it did not add), and the ADR-0087 gate is forward-only (a row already breaking at the merge base is never re-judged), so a new changeset that states "Supersedes, in the same release, the ADR-0087 disposition of the `newTabUrl` narrowing note … now registered" is the one channel that reaches the CHANGELOG reader and the registry. Its text names the superseded note by its summary line, the entry id, both remedies, why neither is mechanical, and the unchanged stored-row behaviour; nothing in it contradicts the merged note's facts. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **No `refused-shapes.ts` detector for the entry** (dev acceptance note) — accepted: the chain emits the entry as a TODO on every hop-18 replay without one (`spec-changes.ts:260`), the precedent entry has none, and the record asked for the D3 entry. A `--stored` row-by-name listing is a lane follow-up, not owed here.
- **The merged `not-required` disposition stays in the merged note** — accepted as above; the superseding paragraph is the correction the release carries.
- **PR body's "the gate reads the `registered` marker"** — should-fix in prose only (the body is not a shipped artifact): the gate skipped a non-breaking changeset; the marker was verified here by hand. No code change.
- **Docs Drift Check (6471576660) names `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`** — answered by `78e8f9751`: the "new-tab target template" wording is replaced with the path rule (judged above). The release-owned `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx` it also names is read-only and still true (it records the pair co-constraint, not the value rule). No further change.
- **`skills/objectstack-ui/evals` case for `newTabUrl`** — stays with the lane seat, as recorded on #27252.
- **Not Tier H** — no governed path on the file list; the head is the thread's own same-repo branch `claude/project-thread-ev6wfx`, one commit on `7858c1d16`; the PR is draft and lands through the queue once ready.
